_about: Case studies for the demo-film selector. CRAFT ANALYSIS ONLY — structural function, directorial decisions, why a technique works. No scene-by-scene plot summaries and no quoted dialogue: a study you could follow instead of watching the film is both a worse lesson and not ours to publish. Schema and validate() live in src/lib/studies.js. Hand-written; npm run extract does not touch this file.

beatSheetMethods.name: Save the Cat
beatSheetMethods.attribution: Blake Snyder's fifteen-beat sheet, from Save the Cat! (2005)

beats.label: Opening Image
beats.function: One image that states the before — the world and the flaw, in a form the ending can answer.
beats.functionTanglish: Padam aarambikkum podhu hero-oda ulagamum avan kuraiyum oru single image-la. Kadaisi katchi adhukku badhil sollura maadhiri irukkanum.

beats.label: Theme Stated
beats.function: Someone says the lesson aloud, early, to a hero not ready to hear it.
beats.functionTanglish: Padathoda paadam yaaravadhu vaayaala sollidraanga, aarambathulaye - kekka innum thayaraaga illaadha hero kitta.

beats.label: Set-Up
beats.function: Show what needs fixing, and the stasis that will not fix it.
beats.functionTanglish: Enna sari pannanum, adha sari pannaama nikkura nilamai enna - rendaiyum kaatnum.

beats.label: Catalyst
beats.function: The knock at the door. Something makes the old life untenable.
beats.functionTanglish: Kadhava thattura sambavam. Pazhaya vaazhkaiya thodara mudiyaadhapadi edho onnu nadakkudhu.

beats.label: Debate
beats.function: The hero resists. The question of the film is asked and not yet answered.
beats.functionTanglish: Hero thayangraan. Padathoda kelvi kekkapadudhu, badhil innum illa.

beats.label: Break Into Two
beats.function: The hero chooses the new world. The choice must be active.
beats.functionTanglish: Hero pudhu ulagatha thernthedukraan. Adhu oru seyalaa irukkanum, avanukku nadakkura sambavamaa illa.

beats.label: B Story
beats.function: The relationship that carries the theme while the A story carries the plot.
beats.functionTanglish: Mudhanmai kadhai aasaiya sumakkum podhu, theme-a sumakkura relationship.

beats.label: Fun and Games
beats.function: The promise of the premise. What the poster sold, delivered.
beats.functionTanglish: Kadhaikkaru enna vaakkuruthi kudutthudho adhu kedaikkura edam. Poster vittadhu ingaye kedaikkum.

beats.label: Midpoint
beats.function: A false victory or a false defeat. Stakes raise, the clock starts.
beats.functionTanglish: Poyyaana vetri illa poyyaana thotru. Pandhayam koodudhu, clock odha aarambikkudhu.

beats.label: Bad Guys Close In
beats.function: Internal and external pressure converge. Whatever was holding frays.
beats.functionTanglish: Ullaiyum veliyilum azhutham serndhu varudhu. Ippadi varaikkum thaangi nindradhu edhuvo adhu vedikka aarambikkudhu.

beats.label: All Is Lost
beats.function: The low point. Often a whiff of death — something ends.
beats.functionTanglish: Romba keezha iruntha point. Podhuvaa edho onnu sagudhu.

beats.label: Dark Night of the Soul
beats.function: The hero sits in the wreckage before the idea arrives.
beats.functionTanglish: Yosanai varadhukku munnadi, thaan undaakkina idipaattukkulla hero okkaandhirukkura neram.

beats.label: Break Into Three
beats.function: A and B stories meet. The lesson from the B story solves the A story.
beats.functionTanglish: Mudhanmai kadhaiyum B-kadhaiyum sandhikkudhu. B-kadhai kuduththa paadam mudhanmai kadhaiya theerkudhu.

beats.label: Finale
beats.function: The hero proves the lesson by doing the hard version of the thing they dodged.
beats.functionTanglish: Thavirthu odina adhe velaiya, kadinamaana vazhila senju paadatha nirupikraan.

beats.label: Final Image
beats.function: The after. The opening image, answered.

concept.premise: Two classmates meet again at a school reunion after twenty-two years apart, and have one night in which to account for the lives they actually lived.
concept.hook: It asks a question almost everyone carries privately: what would you say to the person you never got over, if you got exactly one evening and no second chance?
concept.howBuilt: The premise is established before the reunion begins, by showing the protagonist alone and at work for long enough that his ordinariness registers. The film buys its later emotion by spending its first act on a man with no story — so that when the past arrives, the audience already knows precisely what it is interrupting.
concept.yourTurn: State your premise as a question your audience has already asked themselves, then name the one constraint that forces an answer — a deadline, a single night, a closing door. A premise without a constraint is a situation, not a story.

logline.line: When a travel photographer attends his school reunion after twenty-two years, a single night with the classmate he never stopped loving forces him to face the life he chose instead.
logline.protagonist: A travel photographer who has arranged his adult life to avoid the subject
logline.incident: The reunion puts him in a room with her again
logline.conflict: Both have lived twenty-two years that cannot be undone, and neither will say so directly
logline.goal: To get through one night without lying about what it meant
logline.cost: If he stays silent, he loses the only chance to know that it was mutual
logline.yourTurn: Write yours as: WHEN [incident], a [flawed protagonist] must [goal] or [cost]. If you cannot name the cost, you do not yet know why the story ends.

characters.name: Ram
characters.flaw: Mistakes restraint for integrity — he will not ask for anything he is not offered
characters.need: To find out that he was loved back, and to be able to hear it
characters.external: The evening ends and they return to separate lives
characters.internal: He confirms to himself that not asking was the right choice, and stays that way
characters.arc: From a man who protects himself with silence to one who lets himself be told

characters.name: Janaki
characters.flaw: Has built a life that works, and will not pretend it has not
characters.want: To see him and be unharmed by it
characters.need: To say the thing out loud once, for its own sake
characters.external: She carries the unsaid back into a life that has no room for it
characters.internal: She loses the chance to be honest without being unfaithful to her own choices
characters.arc: From guarded warmth to a clear-eyed honesty that costs her nothing she is not willing to pay

beats.label: Opening Image
beats.function: Establish the protagonist's ordinary world and the shape of what is missing from it.
beats.inFilm: The film opens on the protagonist's working solitude rather than on romance, which sets the baseline the rest of the film measures against.
beats.craft: Open on the life the story will interrupt, not on the interruption.

beats.label: Inciting Incident
beats.function: Something arrives that the protagonist cannot ignore and cannot fully control.
beats.inFilm: The reunion is arranged. The incident is social and low-stakes on its surface, which is the point: the pressure is entirely internal.
beats.craft: An inciting incident does not have to be dramatic. It has to be unavoidable.

beats.label: Plot Point 1
beats.function: The protagonist commits, and the story's real question is posed.
beats.inFilm: The two are finally in the same room. From here the film abandons plot almost entirely and runs on the question of whether either will speak plainly.
beats.craft: Once your question is posed, stop adding events. Events after this point dilute rather than build.

beats.label: Midpoint
beats.function: A shift from reacting to acting — the protagonist stops avoiding the subject.
beats.inFilm: The evening moves from a group to the two of them, and the conversation stops being about the past in general and becomes about them specifically.
beats.craft: Shrink the world at the midpoint. Fewer people, smaller rooms, less escape.

beats.label: All Hope Is Lost
beats.function: The cost becomes concrete and the goal looks unreachable.
beats.inFilm: The facts of twenty-two years are stated rather than dramatised. Nothing is destroyed; it is simply established that it is too late, which is worse.
beats.craft: In a romance, the low point is usually information, not catastrophe.

beats.label: Climax
beats.function: The protagonist acts on the need rather than the want.
beats.inFilm: The resolution is verbal and quiet. The film's whole structure exists to make a short exchange carry the weight of an act break.
beats.craft: Earn a small climax with a large setup, and it will read as large.

beats.label: Resolution
beats.function: Show the changed equilibrium and what it cost.
beats.inFilm: The lives resume. The film declines to reward the audience with a reversal, and that refusal is the ending's argument.
beats.craft: An ending that withholds the obvious gift has to give something else instead — here, certainty.

scenes.title: The reunion's first recognition
scenes.how: The dialogue stays on logistics and old classmates while the staging — distance, who looks away first, who speaks to the group instead — carries the actual content.
scenes.why: The audience does the emotional work themselves, which binds them to the scene more tightly than being told would.
scenes.tanglish: Pesuradhu vera, solradhu vera. Dialogue la oru vishayam, kannula innoru vishayam.

scenes.title: Objects standing in for years
scenes.how: Small physical details — what has been kept, what has been replaced — do the work of exposition about two decades.
scenes.why: A kept object is evidence. Evidence is more persuasive than testimony, and faster.
scenes.tanglish: Oru porul vechurundha, adhu pesama ellaam sollidum.

scenes.title: Time as the antagonist
scenes.how: There is no opposing character. The obstacle is elapsed time and the commitments made inside it.
scenes.why: It proves antagonism is a function, not a person: anything that reliably opposes the goal will do.
scenes.tanglish: Villain kidaiyaadhu. Kadandha kaalam thaan edhiri.

directorNotes: Spends the first act establishing ordinariness, so the second act's small gestures read as large.
Keeps the camera still and lets performance carry scenes that a more restless film would cut.
Uses music to mark memory rather than to instruct the audience how to feel about the present.
Refuses the reversal the genre promises, and makes the refusal the point.

beatSheets.note: 96 is the hardest of the four to map, and the mismatch is the lesson. Snyder's sheet assumes a hero who wants something and pursues it; this one wants something he decided long ago not to pursue. Every beat is present and in order, but three are inverted - the Break Into Two is a decision to stay rather than to act, Fun and Games is not fun, and the Finale is a goodbye rather than a win. An inverted beat is a choice; a missing one is a hole. These are choices.
beatSheets.noteTanglish: Naalu padathulaye 96-a thaan indha sheet-oda porutthi paakkuradhu romba kashtam - andha porundhaadha thanmai thaan paadam. Snyder-oda amaippu, edhavadhu venumnu adha thoraththura hero-va edhirpaakkudhu. Ivano, thoraththuradhilla-nu veku kaalam munnaadiye mudivu pannavan. Ellaa kattangalum varisaiya irukku, aana moonu thalakeezh - Break Into Two-la seyalpaduradhu illa thangaradhu; Fun and Games-la fun-e illa; climax-la vetri illa, oru vidai. Thalakeezhaana kattam oru thervu; vidupatta kattam oru kuzhi. Ivai moonum thervugal.

opening-image.inFilm: A travel photographer detours to the school he left as a boy. The image is a man photographing a place instead of being in it - which is what he has done with the whole of his life since.
opening-image.inFilmTanglish: Oru travel photographer, chinna vayasula vittu ponna school-ukku vazhi maari poraan. Oru edathula irukkuradhukku badhilaa adha photo edukkura manushan - andha naal la irundhu than vaazhkkaiya muzhusaa avan senjadhu adhe thaan.
opening-image.craft: If your ending is quiet, your opening image has to be quiet too. A loud open writes a cheque the last scene cannot cash.
opening-image.craftTanglish: Mudivu amaidhiyaa irundhaa, thodakkamum amaidhiyaave irukkanum. Sathhamaana thodakkam ezhudhura cheque-a kadaisi katchiyaala maathha mudiyaadhu.

theme-stated.inFilm: Stated by a building rather than a person. The school has not changed and he has; the film puts the argument in the production design and never says it out loud.
theme-stated.inFilmTanglish: Oru aalu illa, oru kattidam theme-a solludhu. School maaravillai, avan maariyaachu. Padam andha vaadhatha art department mulamaa vachudradhu, vaayaala oru naalum solradhe illa.
theme-stated.craft: A theme can be stated by production design. If the set contradicts the character, you do not need the line.
theme-stated.craftTanglish: Theme-a set design-e sollalaam. Kalam character-ukku murana nindraa, vasanam thevaiyillai.

set-up.inFilm: Expanded far past the template. The first act is largely a man with no story - solitary, competent, unremarkable. That is the investment: the film is buying the size of the interruption before the interruption arrives.
set-up.inFilmTanglish: Template edhirpaakkuradha vida romba neelam. Mudhal act muzhusum kadhaiye illaadha oru manushan - thaniya, thiramaiyaa, sirappedhum illaama. Adhu thaan mudhaleedu: kurukkeedu varadhukku munnadiye adhoda alava padam vilaikku vaangudhu.
set-up.craft: The longer you can hold an unremarkable present, the more the past costs when it walks in. This is the one beat worth overspending on.
set-up.craftTanglish: Sirappatra nigazhkaalatha evvalavu neram thaanga mudiyudho, avvalavu kanamaa kadandha kaalam ulle nuzhaiyum. Selavu panna thagudhiyaana ore kattam idhu thaan.

catalyst.inFilm: A class group and a reunion date - and the possibility, not the certainty, that she will come. The conditional is deliberate: it turns the next stretch from hesitation into hope.
catalyst.inFilmTanglish: Oru class group, oru reunion thedhi - aval varuvaanu urudhi illa, varalaam-nu oru saathhiyam mattum. Andha nibandhanai vendumnu thaan - adutha pakudhiya thayakkamaa illaama nambikkaiyaa maathhudhu.
catalyst.craft: A conditional catalyst buys you a debate for free. 'She might come' is a whole act; 'she is coming' is a scene.
catalyst.craftTanglish: 'Varalaam'-nu oru thoonduko oru debate-a ilavasamaa kudukkudhu. 'Aval varalaam' oru act; 'aval varraa' oru katchi.

debate.inFilm: Runs as travel. The film puts the question inside a journey, so the protagonist is visibly moving toward a thing he has not agreed to do.
debate.inFilmTanglish: Payanamaave nadakkudhu. Kelviya oru payanathukkulla vachudradhaala, oppukkalaadha ondra nokki hero nagaradhu kannukku theriyudhu.
debate.craft: Give a passive hero a vehicle. Motion reads as intention even when the character has not formed one.
debate.craftTanglish: Seyalatra hero-kku oru vaaganam kudunga. Ulle nokkam uruvaagaama irundhaalum, nagaradhu nokkamaave vaasikkapadum.

break-into-two.inFilm: Inverted. He does not choose to act - he chooses to stay in the room. The active decision the template asks for is there; what it commits him to is looking, not pursuing.
break-into-two.inFilmTanglish: Thalakeezh. Seyalpadanum-nu mudivu panniradhilla - andha arailaye thangaradhaa mudivu panraan. Template kekkura seyal thervu irukku; aana adhu avana kattupaduthuradhu thoraththuradhukku illa, paakkuradhukku.
break-into-two.craft: A passive protagonist still needs an active choice. Let them choose to remain somewhere painful; that is a decision, and it is dramatic.
break-into-two.craftTanglish: Seyalatra hero-kkum oru seyal thervu thevai. Valikkura oru edathula thangaradhaa avan mudivu pannattum - adhuvum oru mudivu thaan, naadagamaanadhum thaan.

b-story.inFilm: Not a character but a timeline. The 1994 thread carries the theme while the present carries the plot, and it is cast with different actors - so the B story is literally a second set of faces making the emotional argument.
b-story.inFilmTanglish: Oru character illa, oru kaala kattam. 1994 izhai theme-a sumakkudhu, nigazhkaalam kadhaiya sumakkudhu. Vera nadigargal - so B-story-nu solradhu ungalukku unmaiyileye vera oru mugak koottam nadathhura unarvu vaadham.
b-story.craft: A B story does not have to be a person. A second timeline, a parallel case, a recurring object - anything that can hold the theme while the A story holds the want.
b-story.craftTanglish: B-story oru nabaraave irukkanum-nu avasiyam illa. Innoru kaala kattam, inaiyaana oru vazhakku, thirumba thirumba varra oru porul - theme-a sumakka koodiya edhuvum sari.

fun-and-games.inFilm: The reunion, and the only genuinely light stretch in the picture. It delivers the promise of the premise as group warmth rather than as romance - which keeps the two of them surrounded, and unable to say anything that matters.
fun-and-games.inFilmTanglish: Reunion - padathula unmaiyaa ilagaana ore pakudhi. Kaadhalaa illaama koottathu anbaa kadhaikkaru-oda vaakkuruthiya nireverudhu - adhanaala avanga rendu perum koottathukku naduvula, mukkiyamaana edhaiyum solla mudiyaama nikkiraanga.
fun-and-games.craft: If your premise promises an intimate conversation, spend Fun and Games making it impossible. The audience will want the midpoint badly.
fun-and-games.craftTanglish: Unga kadhaikkaru oru nerungiya uraiyaadala vaakkuruthi kuduthaa, Fun and Games-a adha saathhiyamatradhaakka selavu pannunga. Midpoint-ukkaaga audience yengiduvaanga.

midpoint.inFilm: A false victory, and a structural narrowing: the ensemble falls away and the film becomes a two-hander. Nothing is won except time alone - which is exactly what raises the stakes.
midpoint.inFilmTanglish: Poyyaana vetri - melum oru amaippu surukkam: koottam vilaga, padam rendu per kadhaiyaa maarudhu. Thaniyaana neram thavira vera edhuvum kedaikkala - adhu thaan pandhayatha uyarthhudhu.
midpoint.craft: A midpoint can change the size of the cast rather than the size of the problem. Going from many to two is a stakes raise.
midpoint.craftTanglish: Midpoint pirachanaiyoda alava maathhaama, koottathoda alava maathhalaam. Palaril irundhu rendu peraa surunguradhum oru pandhaya uyarvu thaan.

bad-guys-close-in.inFilm: The antagonist is a departure time and a life already built elsewhere. Neither can be argued with, which is why the film never gives either of them a scene to be argued with in.
bad-guys-close-in.inFilmTanglish: Edhiri-nu solradhu oru purapadum neram, appuram yaarkanave vera edathula kattapatta oru vaazhkkai. Rendodum vaadhikka mudiyaadhu - adhanaala thaan avatrukku entha katchiyaiyum padam kudukkala.
bad-guys-close-in.craft: The strongest antagonist in a romance is a schedule. It cannot be persuaded, defeated, or made to behave badly.
bad-guys-close-in.craftTanglish: Kaadhal kadhaila romba valimaiyaana edhiri oru time-table thaan. Adha sammadhikka vaikka mudiyaadhu, vella mudiyaadhu, kettavanaavum kaatta mudiyaadhu.

all-is-lost.inFilm: He admits he was at her wedding, standing at the back. She admits she felt it, and had hoped he would stop it. The low point is not that they parted - it is the confirmation that it was reversible, and that both of them let the moment pass.
all-is-lost.inFilmTanglish: Aval kalyaanathula pinnaadi nindradha avan oppukraan. Thaan adha unarndhadhaagavum, avan adha nirutthanum-nu edhirpaathadhaagavum aval solraa. Pirinjadhu thaazhvu pulli illa - adha maathha mudinjirukkum-nu urudhi aaguradhum, andha kanaththa rendu perume kadandhu poga vittaanga-nu theriyuradhum thaan.
all-is-lost.craft: The cruellest low point is proof that the loss was avoidable. Grief over fate is soft; grief over a choice is not.
all-is-lost.craftTanglish: Romba kodiya thaazhvu pulli - izhapa thavirthirukka mudinjirukkum-nu aadhaaram. Vidhiya patthi azhuradhu menmaiyaanadhu; thervu patthi azhuradhu illai.

dark-night.inFilm: The apartment, and the archive - a uniform, dried flowers, poems. Almost no plot advances; the beat is carried by domestic action and by what neither of them says.
dark-night.inFilmTanglish: Andha veedu, appuram andha sekarippu - oru seerudai, ularndha pookal, kavidhaigal. Kadhai kittathatta nagaraadhu; veetu velaigalum, rendu perum sollaadhadhum thaan indha kattatha sumakkudhu.
dark-night.craft: Withhold plot entirely for one sequence. If the preceding hour has worked, the audience will supply the interior monologue themselves.
dark-night.craftTanglish: Oru varisaikku kadhaiyaiye nagarthaama vidunga. Mundhaya oru mani neram velai senjirundhaa, ulmana vasanatha audience-e nirappikkuvaanga.

break-into-three.inFilm: The two timelines meet. She tells him to go on and live, and she sings the song she promised in 1994 - the B story discharging its unfinished obligation so the A story can end.
break-into-three.inFilmTanglish: Rendu kaala kattangalum sandhikkidhu. Vaazhndhu munneru-nu solraa; 1994-la vaakkuruthi kuduththa paadala paadraa - B-kadhai than nireverraadha kadamaiya mudichuvaikka, mudhanmai kadhai mudiya vazhi pirakkudhu.
break-into-three.craft: When your B story is a timeline, Break Into Three is the moment the past hands the present an instruction.
break-into-three.craftTanglish: B-kadhai oru kaala kattamaa irukkum podhu, kadandha kaalam nigazhkaalathukku oru kattalaiya kudukkura tharunam thaan Break Into Three.

finale.inFilm: Inverted, and the film is built for it. The hard version of the thing he dodged at sixteen is not a declaration - it is a goodbye said properly, in person, on time. So the climax is an airport run in reverse.
finale.inFilmTanglish: Thalakeezh - adhukkaagave padam kattapattirukku. Padhinaaraam vayasula thavirthadhan kadinamaana vadivam oru kaadhal vaakkumoolam illa - nerila, sariyaana nerathula sollapadum oru vidai. So climax oru thalakeezh airport ottam.
finale.craft: Ask what your hero avoided in the backstory, then make the finale that exact act. It will not always be the bold one.
finale.craftTanglish: Kadandha kadhaila unga hero edha thavirthaan-nu kettu, adhaiye climax-aakkunga. Adhu eppovum thairiyamaana seyalaa irukkaadhu.

final-image.inFilm: He folds the clothes she left and puts them in the case with everything else he kept. The opening image was a man holding a memory; the last is the same man putting it away. Answered, not improved.
final-image.inFilmTanglish: Aval vittu ponna udaigala madichu, micham ellaathodum andha pettila vaikraan. Thodakka katchi oru ninaiva sumandha manushan; irudhi katchi adhe manushan adha thookki vaikkuradhu. Badhil kedaicchadhu, memppattadhu illa.
final-image.craft: A final image can answer the opening without improving on it. 'Resolved' and 'happy' are different promises; pick one and keep it.
final-image.craftTanglish: Irudhi katchi thodakkathukku badhil sollalaam - memppaduththaama. 'Theervu' vera, 'magizhchi' vera. Ondra thernthedutthu adhula nilunga.

concept.premise: A trainee officer who is frightened of the work is partnered with an unforgiving veteran on a methodical murder investigation, and the case can only be solved as fast as his nerve improves.
concept.hook: The suspense engine is not only who did it but whether the investigator can stay in the room. The audience is given two things to worry about, and can guess at only one of them.
concept.howBuilt: Established by giving the rookie a visible, unglamorous physical reaction to the job in the first act and never letting a later scene forgive it. He is then paired with a senior officer who states the rules of the work out loud, so procedure doubles as exposition and as a continuous examination of the junior. By the time the investigation accelerates, a second scoreboard is already running.
concept.yourTurn: Find the second question your thriller can ask alongside 'who'. A procedural answers one question and stops; a procedural fastened to a person who might fail at being present answers two, and only one of them is guessable from the poster.

logline.line: A fearful trainee officer partnered with an unforgiving veteran must out-think a methodical killer before his own nerve, rather than the evidence, ends the investigation.
logline.protagonist: A trainee officer who is competent on paper and unreliable in the room
logline.incident: A posting places him beside the one colleague who will not let him look away
logline.conflict: Every step of the procedure demands precisely the composure he does not have, and the method under investigation rewards patience over force
logline.goal: To stay in the investigation long enough to be useful to it
logline.cost: Another flinch costs the case, the next person in the pattern, and the last version of himself he could still defend
logline.yourTurn: Test your logline by deleting the crime. If nothing personal is still at risk, you have described a plot and not a story — add the internal stake before you add another suspect.

characters.name: Prakash
characters.flaw: Treats his fear as a verdict on what he is rather than a condition he is in
characters.want: To close the case he has been handed by rank rather than by choice
characters.need: To stop borrowing his nerve from the man standing next to him
characters.external: The investigation moves on without him and someone else pays for the delay
characters.internal: He confirms the sentence he has already passed on himself and stays inside it
characters.arc: From a man who looks away on instinct to the one who looks longest

characters.name: Loganathan
characters.flaw: Has built an armour of detachment and can no longer tell it apart from professionalism
characters.want: A partner who can do the job without being carried
characters.need: To admit the work has cost him something, so that coldness stops passing for clarity
characters.external: The method he trusts stops producing an answer in time
characters.internal: He loses the belief that distance is what keeps him intact
characters.arc: From a man who only instructs to one who can be argued with by his own trainee

characters.name: The killer
characters.flaw: A logic so internally consistent that it cannot adapt to anyone willing to reason from inside it
characters.want: To continue an established pattern without interruption
characters.need: Deliberately withheld — the film writes him as a fixed system rather than a wounded man
characters.external: The pattern is interrupted and becomes legible
characters.internal: Nothing, by design; no redemption is offered, which keeps the film's moral weight on the investigators
characters.arc: Flat on purpose. An antagonist who does not move is the ruler the protagonist's movement is measured against.

beats.label: Opening Image
beats.function: Establish the ordinary world and the shape of what is missing from it.
beats.inFilm: The film opens by establishing the investigative machinery as routine and competent, and the protagonist as the least steady thing inside it. Because the room's standard is set first, his unsteadiness reads as a fact about him rather than as atmosphere.
beats.craft: Set the room's standard before you introduce the character who cannot meet it.

beats.label: Inciting Incident
beats.function: Something arrives that the protagonist can neither ignore nor control.
beats.inFilm: The posting itself. The film declines to make the disturbance an atrocity; what breaks the protagonist's normal is an assignment and a partner, which keeps the pressure internal from the first act onward.
beats.craft: When the plot is already supplying horror, let the inciting incident supply the personal obligation instead.

beats.label: Plot Point 1
beats.function: The protagonist commits, and the story's real question is posed.
beats.inFilm: The search narrows from a general hunt to a specific method, locking the team into a way of working that only patience can sustain. The commitment looks procedural, but because the protagonist's weakness is composure under duration, committing to the method is the same act as committing to his own examination.
beats.craft: Choose an act-two method that is made out of your protagonist's weakness. Then the plot cannot advance without the arc advancing.

beats.label: Midpoint
beats.function: A turn from reacting to acting, and a shift in what the story is actually about.
beats.inFilm: The midpoint invalidates the shape of the investigation rather than adding to it. What the team believed it was solving stops existing, and from that point the protagonist starts generating theories instead of receiving them.
beats.craft: A midpoint that deletes an assumption beats one that adds information. The audience has to re-read everything it has seen, and re-reading feels like acceleration.

beats.label: All Hope Is Lost
beats.function: The cost becomes concrete and the goal looks unreachable.
beats.inFilm: The low point arrives as a loss of standing rather than as a set piece. The protagonist's own worst estimate of himself is confirmed where others can see it, and the film lets that verdict sit without offering comfort. Nothing is destroyed; what is taken away is his permission to continue.
beats.craft: Take the protagonist's authority rather than his safety. Authority is harder to win back, and it costs nothing to shoot.

beats.label: Climax
beats.function: The protagonist acts on the need rather than the want.
beats.inFilm: The case turns on a deduction the protagonist has to make alone, without the person he has been borrowing courage from. The film sequences it so the arc completes first and the case closes as a consequence, not the other way round.
beats.craft: Make the plot's solution require the exact capacity the character lacked in act one, and the ending will feel inevitable instead of clever.

beats.label: Resolution
beats.function: Show the changed equilibrium and what it cost to reach it.
beats.inFilm: The film declines to celebrate. Its closing movement treats the work as continuing and the protagonist as changed but marked, which keeps the theme — that sustained attention has a price — intact through the last frame.
beats.craft: If your theme says courage costs something, the resolution should still be showing the invoice.

scenes.title: Procedure as a character test
scenes.how: The rules of the work are explained to the trainee by the senior officer, so the audience is briefed while a character is being examined on the same material.
scenes.why: Exposition a character can fail at stops being exposition. It becomes conflict with information attached, and nobody checks their phone during it.
scenes.tanglish: Rules sollumbodhu, oruthan test aagitu irukkanum. Appo thaan exposition-um drama aagum.

scenes.title: A detail that is a character note first
scenes.how: The observation that eventually matters is introduced while the scene is ostensibly about something else, and is framed as a quirk of a person rather than as evidence.
scenes.why: An audience filters constantly for relevance. Hide the plant inside characterisation and it slips past the filter, then detonates on the second viewing.
scenes.tanglish: Clue-a clue maadhiri kaatinaa adhu clue illa, announcement. Character detail maadhiri vechaa thaan velai seiyum.

scenes.title: Withholding the frame, not the facts
scenes.how: The mechanics of the investigation are shown openly; only the arrangement that makes them mean something is held back.
scenes.why: Surprise lasts a second, suspense lasts a reel. Keeping the pieces visible and the pattern hidden buys the second without giving up the first.
scenes.tanglish: Ellaam kaamikkalaam. Edhu edhoda sambandham-nu mattum sollaama vidu.

directorNotes: Casts the senior officer as the film's standard of composure, so the junior has something to be measured against in every frame.
Keeps the violence largely off screen and spends the running time on waiting, which is where this genre's tension actually lives.
Lets sound design carry information the dialogue refuses to state, so the audience is listening as hard as the investigators.
Writes an antagonist with a private, coherent logic rather than an appetite — a system can be reasoned toward, and a reasoning protagonist needs one.
Times the final deduction to the completion of the arc rather than to the availability of evidence.

beatSheets.note: Of the four, this is the film the template fits best, and that is worth knowing: the investigative thriller is the form Snyder's sheet was effectively reverse-engineered from, so the beats land close to their marks even at Tamil runtime. Read this one to see the template working cleanly, then read 96 to see what happens when a film argues with it. One structural note before you start: the false solution arrives at the midpoint and is dismantled immediately, which is what buys the back half its dread.
beatSheets.noteTanglish: Naalu padathula indha sheet romba sariyaa porundhuradhu idhukku thaan - adhuvum theriyanum. Snyder-oda amaippu kittathatta investigative thriller-la irundhu thaan pirichu eduthhadhu maadhiri. Adhanaala Tamil runtime-lum kattangal thangal edathukku pakkathula vandhu vizhudhu. Template sutthamaa velai seiradha paakka idha padinga; appuram padam adhoda sandai poduna enna aagum-nu paakka 96 padinga. Oru amaippu kurippu: poyyaana theervu midpoint-la varudhu, udanadiyaa pirichu podapadudhu - adhu thaan pin paadhikku andha bayatha vaangi kudukkudhu.

opening-image.inFilm: The threat is introduced as a method, not as a person - pattern first, perpetrator withheld. The image tells you this film will be about reading evidence rather than chasing a face.
opening-image.inFilmTanglish: Achchuruthhal oru aalaa illa, oru muraiyaa arimugam aagudhu - mudhalla pattern, kolaiyaali maraikkapadraan. Indha padam oru mugatha thoraththuradhu pathi illa, aadhaaratha vaasikkuradhu pathi-nu andha katchiye sollidudhu.
opening-image.craft: In a thriller, your opening image should state the genre of your antagonist. A method promises deduction; a face promises pursuit.
opening-image.craftTanglish: Thriller-la, unga thodakka katchi edhiri-oda vagaiya sollanum. Oru murai deduction-a vaakkuruthi kudukkudhu; oru mugam thuraththala vaakkuruthi kudukkudhu.

theme-stated.inFilm: The film's real argument is that a killer is made, not born - and it is planted early, in the way the veteran insists on asking why rather than only who. The rookie treats it as philosophy. It turns out to be method.
theme-stated.inFilmTanglish: Kolaiyaali piranthadhu illa, uruvaakkapadraan - idhu thaan padathoda unmaiyaana vaadham. Idhu aarambathulaye vaikkapadudhu: 'yaaru'-nu mattum illaama 'yen'-nu kekkanum-nu senior valiyuruthhuraaru. Rookie adha philosophy-nu ninaikkiraan. Kadaisila adhu thaan method-aa maarudhu.
theme-stated.craft: State the theme as the mentor's working habit, not as a speech. Then act three can prove it by using it.
theme-stated.craftTanglish: Theme-a oru pechaa illaama, mentor-oda velai pazhakkamaa sollunga. Appo act three adha upayogichu nirupikkalaam.

set-up.inFilm: A trainee DSP is attached to a veteran SP and a technical assistant. His inexperience is established against the veteran's instinct - not as comedy, but as a gap the case will eventually force him to close alone.
set-up.inFilmTanglish: Oru trainee DSP-ya oru senior SP-kkum oru technical assistant-kkum udan anuppraanga. Senior-oda unarvukku edhira avanoda anubhavamenmai nirupikkapadudhu - comedy-aa illa, kadaisila avane thaniya moodavendiya oru edaiveliyaa.
set-up.craft: Set-Up is an armoury. Any gap you name in the first ten pages should be the thing that closes in the last ten.
set-up.craftTanglish: Set-Up oru aayudha kidangu. Mudhal patthu page-la neenga peru solra edaiveli, kadaisi patthula moodapadanum.

catalyst.inFilm: More young women killed the same way. The catalyst is not a single body but a repetition - the moment the case stops being a crime and becomes a pattern.
catalyst.inFilmTanglish: Adhe muraila innum sila ilam pengal kolai. Thoonduko oru udal illa, oru thirumba nadakkudhal - vazhakku oru kutram-aa irukkuradha nirutthi oru pattern-aa maarura tharunam.
catalyst.craft: In a procedural the catalyst is often the second one. Repetition is what converts an incident into a story.
catalyst.craftTanglish: Procedural-la thoonduko podhuvaa rendaavadhu sambavam thaan. Thirumba nadakkuradhu thaan oru sambavatha kadhaiyaa maathhudhu.

debate.inFilm: Played as visible inadequacy in the field rather than as internal deliberation. The film externalises 'can he do this' by making him fail at small things in front of people who notice.
debate.inFilmTanglish: Ullukkulla yosikkuradhaa illaama, field-la theriyura thiramai kuraivaa kaattapadudhu. 'Ivanaala mudiyuma' kelviya, kavanikkura aalunga munnaadi chinna chinna vishayangalla avana thole vaippadhu mulamaa padam veliya kondu varudhu.
debate.craft: Dramatise the debate as small public failures. It plays faster than doubt and it earns the later competence.
debate.craftTanglish: Debate-a chinna public thoalvigalaa kaattunga. Sandhehatha vida adhu vegamaa odum, appuram varra thiramaikku vilaiyaavum amaiyum.

break-into-two.inFilm: The 1970s cold cases surface and the investigation becomes historical as well as current. He stops asking to be excused and starts working two timelines at once.
break-into-two.inFilmTanglish: 1970-kalla moodapatta vazhakkugal veliya varudhu; vichaaranai nigazhkaalam mattumilla, varalaatru vichaaranaiyaavum aagudhu. Thann vidungappa-nu kekkuradha nirutthittu, rendu kaala kattangalaiyum onnaa velai seiya aarambikraan.
break-into-two.craft: A good act break adds a dimension rather than a destination. The hero is not somewhere new; the case is.
break-into-two.craftTanglish: Nalla act break oru pudhu edathai illa, oru pudhu parimaanatha serkkudhu. Hero pudhu edathukku pogala; vazhakku poidhu.

b-story.inFilm: The mentor pairing, and it carries the whole thematic argument. The veteran is not a source of clues but a position on the theme - what the work costs, and who is allowed to be shaken by it.
b-story.inFilmTanglish: Mentor jodi - idhu thaan theme vaadham muzhusaiyum sumakkudhu. Senior oru clue kidangu illa, theme-la oru nilaipaadu - indha velai enna vilai kekkudhu, adhula kalangura urimai yaarukku irukku.
b-story.craft: In a two-hander procedural, make the partner the theme and the case the plot. Then the case can be solved and the argument still has somewhere to go.
b-story.craftTanglish: Rendu per procedural-la, partner-a theme-aavum vazhakka plot-aavum vachukkonga. Appo vazhakku theerndhaalum vaadhathukku innum poga edam irukkum.

fun-and-games.inFilm: The procedure itself - records, interviews, a borrowed book, a house searched. The film trusts the audience to find method satisfying and refuses to decorate it with action.
fun-and-games.inFilmTanglish: Nadaimurai thaan - aavanangal, vichaaranaigal, oru irval puththagam, oru veedu sodhanai. Muraiye thrupthi tharum-nu audience mela padam nambikkai vaikkudhu; action vachu adha azhagupaduththa maruthudhu.
fun-and-games.craft: If your premise is an investigation, Fun and Games is the investigation. Resist the urge to put a chase in it.
fun-and-games.craftTanglish: Unga kadhaikkaru oru vichaaranai-nna, Fun and Games-um andha vichaaranai thaan. Naduvula oru thuraththal vaikkanum-nu thonradha kattupaduththunga.

midpoint.inFilm: A confession - and the wrong one. A suspect admits to the older killings, which appears to close the case and in fact closes only half of it. The stakes raise because the present killer is still out there and now has a teacher.
midpoint.inFilmTanglish: Oru oppudhal - aana thappaana oppudhal. Pazhaya kolaigala oruthar oppukraar; vazhakku mudinjadhu maadhiri theriyudhu, unmaiyila padhi thaan mudinjirukku. Pandhayam koodudhu - ippo irukkura kolaiyaali innum veliya irukkaan, avanukku oru aasiriyarum irukkaaru.
midpoint.craft: The strongest midpoint answers the question and asks a worse one in the same scene. A solved half is scarier than an open whole.
midpoint.craftTanglish: Romba valimaiyaana midpoint ore katchila kelvikku badhil sollidu, innum modamaana oru kelviya kekkum. Padhi theerndha vazhakku, muzhusaa thirandhirukkura vazhakka vida bayamaanadhu.

bad-guys-close-in.inFilm: The search narrows and the danger widens - proximity now threatens the people around the investigation, not just the investigators. The pressure stops being professional.
bad-guys-close-in.inFilmTanglish: Thedal surungudhu, aabathhu virivadaiyudhu - nerukkam ippo vichaaranai seiyuravanga mattumilla, avanga chuthhi irukkuravangalaiyum achchuruthhudhu. Azhutham thozhil rithiyaana azhuthamaa illaama poidhu.
bad-guys-close-in.craft: Convert the stakes from 'will they solve it' to 'who will they lose'. The first is curiosity; the second is dread.
bad-guys-close-in.craftTanglish: 'Idha theerpaangala' -la irundhu 'yaara izhakka poraanga'-kku pandhayatha maathhunga. Mudhalaavadhu aarvam; rendaavadhu bayam.

all-is-lost.inFilm: The one living link to the present killer removes himself, and takes the trail with him. The low point is not a defeat in a fight - it is an investigation with nothing left to follow.
all-is-lost.inFilmTanglish: Ippo irukkura kolaiyaalikkaana uyirodu irundha ore thodarpu thaane vilagikradhu; adhodu thadamum poidhu. Thaazhvu pulli oru sandaila thotradhu illa - thodara edhuvume illaadha oru vichaaranai.
all-is-lost.craft: Kill the lead, not the hero. An investigation with nowhere to go is a lower point than an investigator who is hurt.
all-is-lost.craftTanglish: Hero-va illa, thadatha kolunga. Poga edame illaadha vichaaranai, kaayapatta vichaaranaiyaalarai vida aazhamaana thaazhvu pulli.

dark-night.inFilm: The film drops its procedural rhythm entirely - the only stretch in the picture where the case does not move. In a film built on forward motion, stillness is the beat.
dark-night.inFilmTanglish: Padam than procedural thaalatha muzhusaa vittududhu - vazhakku nagaraadha ore pakudhi idhu thaan. Munnokki nagaruradhaale kattapatta oru padathula, asaiyaama nikkuradhe andha kattam thaan.
dark-night.craft: In a film with a strong rhythm, stopping the rhythm is a beat. You do not need a new location or a new character.
dark-night.craftTanglish: Valuvaana thaalam ulla padathula, thaalatha nirutthuradhe oru kattam. Pudhu location-o pudhu character-o thevaiyillai.

break-into-three.inFilm: The method changes from tracing a history to reading a grievance - understanding who this killer selects and why. The mentor's insistence on 'why' becomes the practical tool, which is the B story's argument arriving in the A story's hands.
break-into-three.inFilmTanglish: Murai maarudhu - oru varalaatra thodaruradhu maari, oru kuraiya vaasikkuradhu. Indha kolaiyaali yaara thernthedukraan, yen-nu purinjukuradhu. Mentor 'yen'-nu valiyuruthhinadhu ippo oru nadaimurai karuviyaa aagudhu - B-kadhaioda vaadham mudhanmai kadhai kaila vandhu serudhu.
break-into-three.craft: Break Into Three is where the mentor's habit becomes the hero's instrument. Plant it as an irritation and the reversal costs you nothing.
break-into-three.craftTanglish: Mentor-oda pazhakkam hero-oda karuviyaa maarura edam thaan Break Into Three. Adha oru elarachalaa vidhaicha, andha thirumbal ungalukku onnume selavaagaadhu.

finale.inFilm: The colleague is taken and the pursuit goes into the woods. The mentor is put down and the rookie finishes it - the film is careful that he is not brave, only functional while frightened, which is the harder and truer version.
finale.inFilmTanglish: Oru sagaviththagar kadathhapadraar, thuraththal kaattukkulla poidhu. Mentor kizha thallapadraaru, rookie adha mudikraan - avan thairiyasaali-nu padam kaattala; bayathodaye velai seiraan, adhu thaan kadinamaanadhum unmaiyaanadhum.
finale.craft: Do not cure the flaw in the finale - have the hero work despite it. Cured flaws are wish fulfilment; managed ones are character.
finale.craftTanglish: Climax-la kuraiya kunapaduththaadheenga - adhodaye hero velai seiyattum. Kunamaana kurai oru aasai nirevettram; kaiyaalapatta kurai character.

final-image.inFilm: He gives his music player to a boy in a violent household. Set against an opening that introduced a killer as a method, the last image is the film answering its own theme: if violence is made, it is interrupted early or not at all.
final-image.inFilmTanglish: Vanmurai nirandha oru veetla irukkura oru paiyanukku than music player-a kudukraan. Kolaiyaaliya oru muraiyaa arimugapaduththina thodakkathukku edhira vachu paathaa, irudhi katchi padam thanakku thaane badhil solradhu: vanmurai uruvaakkapaduthu-nna, adha aarambathuleye nirutthanum, illaatti nirutthave mudiyaadhu.
final-image.craft: If your theme says a thing is made, end on someone making a different one. An answer is stronger than a warning.
final-image.craftTanglish: Oru vishayam uruvaakkapadudhu-nu unga theme sonna, vera onna uruvaakkura oruthar kitta mudinga. Eccharikkaiya vida badhil valimaiyaanadhu.

concept.premise: A college dropout who talked his way into a corporate career on a forged degree is recognised by the one man who can prove it, and can only keep the life he invented by going back and actually earning it.
concept.hook: The shortcut is charming and the bill is not. The audience is made complicit in the con for an hour, then handed the invoice at the same moment the protagonist is.
concept.howBuilt: Built by playing the opening movement as comedy and letting the audience enjoy the protagonist's nerve without reservation. The forged credential is introduced as a joke and the count of unfinished papers as a running gag, so when both are re-read as arithmetic the tonal shift arrives as a consequence rather than as a change of genre.
concept.yourTurn: Decide now which of your first-act laughs will be re-read in the third act, and plant it twice. A joke that turns into evidence is the cheapest durable setup there is, because the audience memorised it for fun.

logline.line: A young man living on a forged degree is recognised by his former dean and given one term to clear the papers he never passed, or lose the job, the engagement and the last person still willing to believe him.
logline.protagonist: A young man whose one real talent is being believed, and who has never tested whether he is worth believing
logline.incident: The one man who knows what he actually is recognises him
logline.conflict: The debt is real, the clock is short, and every day spent paying it is a day the invented life can collapse on its own
logline.goal: To convert a lie into a fact before either of his two lives discovers the other
logline.cost: Failure costs the job, the engagement and his father's belief — three separate losses, each with a face attached
logline.yourTurn: Write the cost as three specific people rather than one abstraction. 'He loses everything' is not a stake; 'he loses her, the job, and the only person who ever defended him' is three, and each can be lost separately.

characters.name: Ragavan
characters.flaw: Believes the result is the only thing anybody ever audits
characters.want: Status large enough to be seen by the people who wrote him off
characters.external: Career, marriage and standing dissolve together, because they were all built on the same document
characters.internal: He becomes permanently a man who can only be liked by people who do not know him
characters.arc: From a boy who buys the outcome to a man who chooses the loss that buys the truth

characters.name: The dean
characters.flaw: Cannot tell the difference between enforcing a rule and being right about a person
characters.want: The rule applied without exception to the one student who proved it could be ignored
characters.need: To see what the rule costs and still choose it, with his eyes open
characters.external: The precedent collapses and the institution's word stops meaning anything
characters.internal: He finds out whether his rigour was ever for the students or only for himself
characters.arc: Immovable by design; the film saves whatever yield he has for the latest possible moment, so it reads as earned rather than granted

characters.name: The classmate
characters.flaw: Absorbed a cost that was not his and never billed it to anyone
characters.want: To be left out of somebody else's second chance
characters.need: To be acknowledged, which is not the same thing as being compensated
characters.external: He stays an invisible line item in another man's success
characters.internal: He keeps believing honesty is simply the slower route to the same destination
characters.arc: Static on purpose. The mirror is not there to change; it is there to price the protagonist's choice in a currency the audience can read.

beats.label: Opening Image
beats.function: Establish the ordinary world and the ability the story will test.
beats.inFilm: The film opens in a comic register with the protagonist performing a fluency he does not possess. It establishes the skill that will both save and indict him — persuasion — before it establishes anything he actually knows.
beats.craft: Open on the ability your character will misuse, not on the misuse. Then the audience likes him before it has to judge him.

beats.label: Inciting Incident
beats.function: Something arrives that the protagonist cannot ignore and cannot manage away.
beats.inFilm: Recognition. Everything before it is setup; from the moment he is identified the film has a clock, a creditor and a second life to protect, all obtained from a single encounter.
beats.craft: The strongest inciting incident is a person rather than an event, because a person keeps arriving.

beats.label: Plot Point 1
beats.function: The protagonist commits, and the story's real question is posed.
beats.inFilm: He accepts the terms and re-enters the life he ran from. The commitment is humiliating rather than heroic, which is exactly what lets act two be funny and act three be unarguable.
beats.craft: If the act-one commitment costs dignity instead of safety, comedy and drama can share one spine without either apologising.

beats.label: Midpoint
beats.function: The protagonist stops reacting and starts acting; the goal itself changes shape.
beats.inFilm: The objective converts from concealment to completion — he stops managing the man who knows and starts doing the work. The film marks the turn by changing what a scene is for, from dodging to counting.
beats.craft: At the midpoint, change the verb. Reacting characters hide; acting characters keep score.

beats.label: All Hope Is Lost
beats.function: The cost becomes concrete and the goal looks unreachable.
beats.inFilm: The low point is an accounting rather than an exposure. The protagonist is shown the bill in a form he cannot argue with, and it was paid by somebody who never took the shortcut. The film withholds catastrophe and delivers a reckoning instead.
beats.craft: Let the darkest beat be information the protagonist cannot unlearn, and leave him nobody to blame for it.

beats.label: Climax
beats.function: The protagonist acts on the need rather than the want.
beats.inFilm: He is not caught; he chooses the loss. Routing the ending through a voluntary act means the theme, and not the plot mechanism, gets the last word.
beats.craft: If your theme is about honesty, the climax has to be a choice the protagonist could have avoided. A confession extracted under pressure proves nothing.

beats.label: Resolution
beats.function: Show the changed equilibrium and what it cost.
beats.inFilm: The new life is smaller than the invented one and better founded. The closing movement is careful to present the reduced version as sufficient rather than as a punishment, which is what keeps the film an argument instead of a warning.
beats.craft: A cautionary tale that ends in ruin teaches nobody anything. End on a smaller, real life and the argument holds.

scenes.title: The gag that becomes arithmetic
scenes.how: A number used repeatedly as comic shorthand is later restated as a workload with a deadline attached. Nothing new is introduced; only the register changes.
scenes.why: The audience already memorised the number for free, because it was funny. Payoff costs nothing when the setup was entertaining on its own terms.
scenes.tanglish: Modhal-la comedy-a sollu. Appuram adhey vishayathaiye seriousa sollu — audience mind-la already irukkum.

scenes.title: An antagonist who is simply correct
scenes.how: The opposing character is given a position the audience cannot dismiss and a manner that offers the protagonist nothing to push against.
scenes.why: Malice can be defeated. A correct rule has to be satisfied, and satisfying it is the only thing that makes the protagonist do the work himself.
scenes.tanglish: Villain kitta thappu irundha easy. Avan sollradhu sari-nu aaidhuna thaan hero-kku velai.

scenes.title: Two tones on one subject
scenes.how: Comedy and drama are played on the same material rather than in alternating blocks; the jokes are about the exact thing the drama will later indict.
scenes.why: Tonal shifts break a film when the two tones are about different subjects. Sharing a subject makes the shift read as the audience's understanding deepening rather than as the film losing its nerve.
scenes.tanglish: Comedy-um dramavum rendu vera vishayam-a irundha padam odanjidum. Onnaave irundha, adhu valarchi.

directorNotes: Buys the audience's affection for the con in act one, then charges them for it in act three.
Gives the antagonist a correct position and no cruelty, which quietly removes the easy exit from the plot.
Places the real consequence on a secondary character, so the protagonist's loss is moral rather than merely inconvenient.
Uses a running joke as the film's load-bearing setup, so the most important exposition arrives disguised as entertainment.
Ends on a reduced life presented as sufficient, refusing both the punishment ending and the reward ending.

beatSheets.note: Dragon runs 155 minutes against a sheet written for 110 pages, so the page targets are a ruler the film does not use. What survives the conversion is the order and the job of each beat. Two structural facts are worth having in front of you: the film opens on a boy who has genuinely earned something, and it ends on a man earning something much smaller, honestly. Everything between those two images is the cost of the shortcut taken in between.

opening-image.inFilm: 2014. A diligent twelfth-standard student wins a gold medal in computer science. This matters more than it looks: the film opens on merit that was actually earned, so the forgery later is not a boy who never could, it is a boy who stopped.
opening-image.craft: Give your hero a real achievement before you give them a shortcut. Otherwise the fall is a diagnosis, not a tragedy.
opening-image.inFilmTanglish: 2014. Plus Two-la computer science-la gold medal vaangura oru nalla maanavan. Idhu theriyuradha vida mukkiyam - padam aarambikkuradhe unmaiyaa uzhaichu vaangina thiramaila. Adhanaala apparam varra fake certificate, mudiyaadhavan kadhai illa; nirutthittavan kadhai.
opening-image.craftTanglish: Kurukku vazhi kudukkaradhukku munnadi hero-kku oru unmaiyaana saadhanai kudunga. Illaatti avan vizhuradhu sogam-aa illaama, oru diagnosis maadhiri thaan irukkum.

theme-stated.inFilm: Stated as its own inversion, which is the film's cleverest structural move. The rejection comes with a reason — that being well-mannered is what disqualified him — and the film spends two and a half hours proving that reason wrong.
theme-stated.craft: You can state the theme as a lie. Put the false thesis in act one, let the hero believe it, and the whole film becomes the rebuttal.
theme-stated.inFilmTanglish: Theme-a neraa sollaama, thalakeezhaa solraanga - idhu thaan padathoda romba clever-aana amaippu. Reject pannurathukku oru reason solraanga: nalla paiyanaa irundhadhu thaan kuraiyaam. Andha reason thappunu nirupikkave meedhi rendarai mani neram.
theme-stated.craftTanglish: Theme-a oru poyaavum sollalaam. Thappaana vaadhatha act one-la vachu, hero adha nambattum - appo padame adhukkaana marupp-aa maarum.

set-up.inFilm: The plan is stated aloud and in full — engineering, a masters abroad, then marriage. Naming the whole route in act one is what lets the film measure every later compromise against it.
set-up.craft: Make your hero say the plan out loud early. Every deviation afterwards is then measurable without a line of dialogue.
set-up.inFilmTanglish: Plan-a full-aa, veliyaave solraan - engineering, veliyoorla masters, apparam kalyaanam. Full route-aiyum act one-laye peru solli sonnadhaala thaan, apparam varra ovvoru compromise-aiyum adhoda alandhu paakka mudiyudhu.
set-up.craftTanglish: Hero than plan-a aarambathulaye vaayvittu sollattum. Adhukku appuram ovvoru vilagala-yum oru vasanam kooda illaama audience alandhuduvaanga.

catalyst.inFilm: The rejection. It is personal rather than academic, and the film is precise about the insult: he is turned down for the exact quality the set-up spent ten minutes establishing as a virtue.
catalyst.craft: The sharpest catalyst attacks the trait you just established as good. Same scene, opposite valence.
catalyst.inFilmTanglish: Andha reject. Idhu padippu sambandhamaana vishayam illa, personal. Avamaanam edhula-nu padam romba clear-aa irukku - set-up-la patthu nimisham nalla gunam-nu kaattina adhe vishayathukkaaga thaan avan reject pannapadraan.
catalyst.craftTanglish: Nalladhu-nu neenga ippo thaan nirupicha guna-thaiye thaakkuradhu thaan koormaiyaana catalyst. Adhe vishayam, ethir madhippu.

debate.inFilm: Almost absent, and deliberately. He does not weigh anything — he converts humiliation straight into a new identity. The missing deliberation is the characterisation.
debate.craft: If your character would not deliberate, do not make them. A skipped debate characterises — as long as the skip is visible.
debate.inFilmTanglish: Kittathatta illave illa - adhuvum vendumnu thaan. Avan edhaiyum yosikkala; avamaanatha neraa oru pudhu adayaalamaa maathikraan. Yosikkaadhadhu thaan avanoda character.
debate.craftTanglish: Unga character yosikkura aalu illaatti, yosikka vaikkaadheenga. Thavirkkapatta debate-um oru characterisation thaan - andha thavirppu theriyum-naa.

break-into-two.inFilm: He becomes "Dragon". The act-two choice is an identity, not a plan — he does not decide to do anything in particular, he decides to be someone else, and the arrears follow from that rather than from any scheme.
break-into-two.craft: A Break Into Two can be a change of self rather than a change of goal. Plot then arrives as consequence, which is harder to write and better to watch.
break-into-two.inFilmTanglish: Avan 'Dragon' aagraan. Act two-oda thervu oru plan illa, oru adayaalam - kurippa edhaiyum seiyya mudivu pannala, vera oruthanaa irukka mudivu panraan. Arrears ellaam adhoda vilaivu thaan, edho thittathoda vilaivu illa.
break-into-two.craftTanglish: Break Into Two-va goal maatramaa illaama suya maatramaa-vum vechukkalaam. Appo kadhai vilaivaa varum - ezhudha kashtam, paakka super.

b-story.inFilm: Keerthi. The college relationship carries the thematic argument while the A story is busy being funny — she is the one who keeps asking what he intends to become, which is the question the dean will later ask with authority behind it.
b-story.craft: Let the B story ask the question the authority figure will later enforce. Same question, two volumes.
b-story.inFilmTanglish: Keerthi. Mudhanmai kadhai comedy-la mulgi irukkum podhu theme-a sumakkuradhu indha college relationship thaan - 'nee enna aaga poara?'-nu thodarndhu kekkuradhu aval. Apparam adhe kelviya thaan dean authority-oda kekkuraaru.
b-story.craftTanglish: Authority-kaaran apparam valiyuruthha poara adhe kelviya B-story munnadiye kekkattum. Ore kelvi, rendu volume.

fun-and-games.inFilm: The college era with Anbu — notoriety, played broad and for laughs. The forty-eight arrears accumulate here as a running joke, which is exactly why the number lands like a sentence when it is read back to him later.
fun-and-games.craft: Accumulate your third-act problem as a first-half joke. The audience laughed at the number; they will feel complicit when it is totalled.
fun-and-games.inFilmTanglish: Anbu-vodu college kaalam - peru ketta kaalam, comedy-aa, periya scale-la. Nappatthettu arrears inga oru thodar joke-aa thaan serudhu. Adhanaala thaan apparam adhe number avan munnaadi vaasikkapadum podhu oru thandanai maadhiri vizhudhu.
fun-and-games.craftTanglish: Third act problem-a first half-la joke-aa serthu vainga. Andha number-a paathu sirichavanga, adhu total pannum podhu thangalukkum pangu irukku-nu feel pannuvaanga.

midpoint.inFilm: A false victory. The forged degree gets him into the company and he is genuinely good at the job — the film is careful that the competence is real and only the credential is fake, which is what makes the rest of the story an argument rather than a lecture.
midpoint.craft: Make the lie unnecessary. If your hero could have done it honestly, the audience argues with itself for the rest of the film.
midpoint.inFilmTanglish: Poyyaana vetri. Fake certificate avana company-kkulla kondu poidudhu; aana velaila avan unmaiyaave kalakraan. Thiramai unmai, certificate mattum thaan poi - idhula padam romba careful-aa irukku. Adhanaala thaan meedhi kadhai oru lecture-aa illaama oru vaadham-aa nikkudhu.
midpoint.craftTanglish: Poi thevaiyillaadhadhaa irukkattum. Nermaiyaave avan saadhichirukka mudiyum-naa, meedhi padam full-um audience thanakkullaye vaadhaadikittu irupaanga.

bad-guys-close-in.inFilm: Promotions, a proposal, a life assembling itself at speed — and then the dean, who has the one document that undoes all of it. The ultimatum starts a three-month clock, which is the film finally giving its shapeless guilt a deadline.
bad-guys-close-in.craft: Give guilt a deadline. Remorse without a date on it does not build, it just repeats.
bad-guys-close-in.inFilmTanglish: Promotion-gal, oru kalyaana pechu, vegamaa kattamaiyura vaazhkai - apparam dean, idhu ellaathaiyum azhikkakoodiya ore document-oda. Andha ultimatum moonu maasa clock-a start pannudhu. Vadivam illaadha kutha unarvukku padam kadaisila oru deadline kudukkudhu.
bad-guys-close-in.craftTanglish: Kutha unarvukku oru deadline kudunga. Thedhi illaadha varutham valaraadhu, thirumba thirumba varum, adhoda sari.

all-is-lost.inFilm: Not the exposure — the harm. An answer-sheet swap during the arrears attempt costs a classmate a job offer, and the protagonist has now done to someone else a version of the thing that was done to him. This is the moral floor of the film, and it is worse than being caught.
all-is-lost.craft: The real low point is not exposure, it is becoming the thing that hurt you. Exposure threatens the hero; this indicts him.
all-is-lost.inFilmTanglish: Ambalam aaguradhu illa - injury panradhu. Arrears exam-la nadakkura answer sheet maatram oru saga maanavanukku kedaicha velaiya pariykkudhu. Thanakku nadandhadhoda oru version-a ippo avan innoruthanukku senjirukkaan. Idhu thaan padathoda moral floor - pidipaduradha vida modam.
all-is-lost.craftTanglish: Unmaiyaana low point ambalam aaguradhu illa - unna kaayapaduthinadhu edhuvo adhuvaa nee maaruradhu. Ambalam hero-va mirattudhu; idhu avana kutravaaliyaakkudhu.

dark-night.inFilm: Guilt, carried quietly, against a wedding that is still scheduled. The film withdraws its comedy almost entirely here — the register shift is how the beat is marked, in a picture that has been funny for two hours.
dark-night.craft: In a comedy, stop being funny. The audience reads the silence faster than any speech about consequences.
dark-night.inFilmTanglish: Kutha unarvu, amaidhiyaa sumakkapadudhu - kalyaanamo innum fix aagiye irukku. Inga padam than comedy-ya muzhusaa eduthududhu. Rendu mani neram sirikka vecha padathula, andha tone maatram thaan indha kattathoda adayaalam.
dark-night.craftTanglish: Comedy padathula, sirikka vekkuradha nirutthunga. Vilaivu pathi pesura entha vasanathaiyum vida andha amaidhiya audience vegamaa purinjupanga.

break-into-three.inFilm: He chooses confession over completion. The ultimatum offered him a way to keep everything by passing the exams; he declines the offered exit, which is the B story’s question finally answered in the A story’s currency.
break-into-three.craft: Offer your hero a clean way out at the act break, then have them refuse it. A refused exit is worth three scenes of resolve.
break-into-three.inFilmTanglish: Exam pass panradha vida oppudhala thernthedukraan. Ellaathaiyum thakka vachukka dean oru vazhi kuduthirundhaaru; andha vazhiya avan maruthudraan. B-story ketta kelvikku, mudhanmai kadhaioda naanayathula kedaicha badhil idhu.
break-into-three.craftTanglish: Act break-la hero-kku oru clean-aana thappikkum vazhi kudunga - apparam adha avan maruthattum. Maruthapatta oru vazhi, uruthi pathi moonu katchikku samam.

finale.inFilm: He confesses before the wedding, surrenders, and serves six months. The film declines every available softening — no reprieve, no technicality, no montage that skips the sentence. The hard version of the thing he dodged is simply the consequence, taken.
finale.craft: If your theme is consequence, film the consequence. Skipping the sentence in a cut tells the audience you did not mean it.
finale.inFilmTanglish: Kalyaanathukku munnadi oppukraan, sarandaraan, aaru maasam jail. Padam kedaikkura entha melladhaana vazhiyaiyum ethukkala - vilakku illa, sattam nunukkam illa, thandanaiya thaandi pora montage illa. Thavirthu odina adhe velai-oda kadinamaana vadivam, vilaiva ethukkuradhu mattum thaan.
finale.craftTanglish: Unga theme 'vilaivu'-nna, andha vilaiva padamaakkunga. Thandanaiya oru cut-la thaandi ponaa, neenga sonnadha neengale nambala-nu audience-ukku theriyum.

final-image.inFilm: After release, a modest delivery job. Set against the gold medal of the opening image it is a precise answer rather than a sad one: the first was merit rewarded, the last is merit rebuilt from nothing, and the film argues the second is worth more.
final-image.craft: Your final image should be smaller than your opening image and worth more. Scale down, value up.
final-image.inFilmTanglish: Veliya vandhadhukku appuram, oru saadhaarana delivery velai. Thodakka katchi-oda gold medal-ukku edhira vachu paathaa idhu soga mudivu illa, sariyaana badhil: mudhalaavadhu thiramaikku kedaicha parisu; kadaisiyadhu poojyathula irundhu thirumba kattina thiramai. Rendaavadhu thaan periyadhu-nu padam vaadhaadudhu.
final-image.craftTanglish: Final image thodakka katchiya vida chinnadhaa irukkattum - aana madhippula periyadhaa. Alavula kurai, madhippula ettru.

beatSheets.noteTanglish: Padam 155 nimisham; indha sheet-a ezhudhinadhu 110 page screenplay-kku. So page number ellaam indha padathukku porundhaadhu. Micham irukkuradhu kattangaloda varisaiyum, ovvondrum senjura velaiyum thaan. Rendu vishayatha manasula vechukkonga: padam aarambikkuradhu unmaiyaa uzhaichu sambadhicha oru paiyan kitta; mudiyuradhu romba chinna onna nermaiyaa sambadhikkura oru manushan kitta. Edaila irukkuradhu ellaam andha kurukku-vazhi-oda vilai.

concept.premise: An encounter cop who has never doubted which side he is on is drawn into a contest with a gangster who will only answer questions by telling stories.
concept.hook: The film hands its antagonist the narration and puts the audience's own moral certainty on trial alongside the protagonist's.
concept.howBuilt: The folk-tale frame is declared at the outset rather than sprung, so the shape of the film is public from the first reel. Each story is then handed over as a deliberate choice by the person telling it, which converts backstory into an act of aggression and makes the audience lean into information it would otherwise sit through.
concept.yourTurn: If your film needs a lot of backstory, give the telling of it to whoever profits from the listener hearing it, and let them pick the moment. Exposition someone wants to deliver is a scene. Exposition nobody wants to deliver is a delay.

logline.line: An encounter cop hunting a gangster finds himself handed three stories that leave him unable to tell his own side from the other one.
logline.protagonist: A police officer whose competence has never been separated from his conviction that he is the good one
logline.incident: The man he is hunting chooses the terms of his own capture
logline.conflict: The antagonist opposes him with an argument rather than with force, and an argument cannot be shot
logline.goal: To finish the hunt cleanly, the way every previous one finished
logline.cost: Losing does not cost him his life; it costs him the right to believe the record he has already filed
logline.yourTurn: Ask what your protagonist would have to stop believing in order to lose. If the answer is 'nothing, he would just die', you have written a chase, not a climax.

characters.name: Vikram
characters.flaw: Has confused a clean record with a clean conscience
characters.want: To find and finish his target, cleanly and on the department's terms
characters.need: To admit that his certainty was a convenience rather than a moral position
characters.external: The case, the unit's standing, and the version of events he has already written down
characters.internal: The self-image that is the only thing making the work bearable
characters.arc: Erodes in three graded stages, one per story, from certainty to a decision he has to make with no cover left

characters.name: Vedha
characters.flaw: Believes a good enough question settles a matter, so he keeps asking instead of answering
characters.want: To be caught, but only on terms he sets
characters.need: To be understood by exactly the one person obliged to condemn him
characters.external: He loses control of the telling and becomes merely a suspect
characters.internal: He loses the only listener capable of grasping what he did and why
characters.arc: Holds his position throughout. He is not the one who changes, which is precisely what makes the protagonist's change measurable.

characters.name: Priya
characters.flaw: Applies a principle without flinching, including to the people she lives with
characters.want: The law applied as it is written rather than as it is convenient
characters.need: To learn whether her principle survives contact with her own household
characters.external: Her professional position becomes untenable at home
characters.internal: She discovers whether her rigour was ever actually tested
characters.arc: The film's control group: she already holds the position the protagonist claims to hold, and the gap between them is the argument.

beats.label: Opening Image
beats.function: Establish the ordinary world, and the belief the story exists to test.
beats.inFilm: The film opens by establishing the protagonist's method as routine, sanctioned and effective, and by inviting the audience to approve of it. The whole argument depends on the audience having agreed with him first.
beats.craft: If your theme is about certainty, spend the opening making the audience share it. You cannot dismantle a belief the audience never held.

beats.label: Inciting Incident
beats.function: Something arrives that the protagonist cannot ignore and cannot control.
beats.inFilm: The hunted man arranges his own capture. The incident is an inversion — the protagonist gets exactly what he wanted and instantly loses authorship of it — and because it is the antagonist's choice rather than luck, the film pays no coincidence tax for it.
beats.craft: An inciting incident the antagonist volunteers costs nothing in contrivance and buys you a character who is already ahead of the plot.

beats.label: Plot Point 1
beats.function: The protagonist commits, and the story's real question is posed.
beats.inFilm: The first story is told and the film's machinery is declared: this will be settled in argument, not in pursuit. The protagonist commits to listening, which is the one activity his method has never required of him.
beats.craft: Make the act-one commitment an activity your protagonist is bad at. Then every scene of act two is both plot and character.

beats.label: Midpoint
beats.function: A turn from reacting to acting, and a change in what is being investigated.
beats.inFilm: The second story lands and the direction of the investigation reverses: the protagonist begins auditing his own record instead of his target's. The film changes the object of the search without changing a single location.
beats.craft: The most economical midpoint changes what is being investigated rather than where. It costs one scene and re-prices every scene before it.

beats.label: All Hope Is Lost
beats.function: The cost becomes concrete and the goal looks unreachable.
beats.inFilm: The low point withdraws the protagonist's institutional cover and his moral cover in the same movement, leaving him a position he can no longer defend from either direction. No external disaster is required; the film has been removing supports since the first story.
beats.craft: Build the low point as the last support being withdrawn. Then it reads as arithmetic the audience did themselves, rather than as a plot event.

beats.label: Climax
beats.function: The protagonist acts on the need rather than the want.
beats.inFilm: The final question is not settled by another story. The film withholds the very device it trained the audience to expect and makes the protagonist answer for himself, which is what turns a structural conceit into a theme.
beats.craft: Take away your own device in the last act. A pattern you break deliberately is the strongest statement that pattern can make.

beats.label: Resolution
beats.function: Show the changed equilibrium and refuse to over-explain it.
beats.inFilm: The ending declines to arbitrate. Both positions remain arguable and the film closes on the protagonist's choice rather than on a verdict about it.
beats.craft: If your theme is that the line moves, do not draw it in the last scene.

scenes.title: A riddle that is really a confession
scenes.how: The antagonist's stories are framed as moral puzzles addressed to the listener while functioning as disclosure about the teller.
scenes.why: The listener has to engage in order to answer, and engaging is how he gets implicated. Subtext that demands a reply is stronger than subtext the audience merely notices.
scenes.tanglish: Kelvi maadhiri kekkuraan, aana adhu confession. Badhil sollavey avan andha kadhaikkulla vandhutaan.

scenes.title: Exposition as an attack
scenes.how: Backstory is delivered only by the character who gains from the listener knowing it, and only at the moment when knowing it costs the listener most.
scenes.why: Information becomes a weapon the second someone chooses when to hand it over. The audience stops tracking facts and starts tracking intent, which is far more watchable.
scenes.tanglish: Thagaval yaaru kudukkuraanga, eppo kudukkuraanga — adhu thaan scene. Suma sonna adhu notice.

scenes.title: A structure announced in advance
scenes.how: The film states its own shape at the start, so the audience knows how many stories are coming and can spend its attention on what each one will cost instead of on what form the next one will take.
scenes.why: Declared structure converts curiosity into suspense. The audience stops guessing the format and starts dreading the content.
scenes.tanglish: Kadhai enna shape-la varum-nu munnadiye sollidu. Appo audience 'enna varum' nu illaama, 'evlo vali kudukkum' nu yosippaanga.

directorNotes: Declares the folk-tale structure in the opening so the audience tracks meaning rather than form.
Gives the antagonist the narration and the better questions, and trusts the protagonist's arc to remain the film's spine anyway.
Keeps the moral argument inside plot mechanics — every debate carries a consequence, so no scene is only a debate.
Withholds the pattern's final repetition, so the last decision cannot be outsourced to another story.
Puts a character who genuinely holds the protagonist's stated principles inside his own house, which makes the hypocrisy legible without a speech.

beatSheets.note: Vikram Vedha is the one film here that announces its own structure before it starts. The Vikram-Betaal frame - a being who poses questions that have more than one right answer - is stated in an animated prologue and then executed literally: the antagonist tells three stories, each ending in a moral question put to the hero. So Fun and Games is nested. Three self-contained tales sit inside the second act, and each one quietly removes a fact the protagonist thought he owned.
beatSheets.noteTanglish: Inga irukkura naalu padathula, than amaippa padam aarambikkuradhukku munnaadiye arivikkura ore padam idhu thaan. Vikramadhithan-Vedhaalam frame - oru kelvikku oru badhilukku mela irukkum-nu solra oru jeevan - animation prologue-la sollapadudhu, appuram adhe padamaave nadakkudhu: edhiri moonu kadhaigal solraan, ovvondrum hero kitta oru arasiyal-thanmai kelvila mudiyudhu. So Fun and Games ullukkulla adukkapattirukku. Rendaam angathukkulla moonu thani kadhaigal, ovvondrum hero thanoda-nu ninaicha oru unmaiya amaidhiyaa eduthuduthu.

opening-image.inFilm: An animated prologue of the old folktale, then an encounter carried out as routine. The image is a man who is certain, doing a certain thing - and a frame that has just told you certainty is the subject.
opening-image.inFilmTanglish: Pazhaya nadodi kadhai animation-la, appuram oru encounter - vazhakkamaana velai maadhiri. Katchi-nu paatha: urudhiyaana oru manushan, urudhiyaana oru velaiya seiraan - appuram andha urudhi thaan padathoda vishayam-nu ippo thaan sonna oru frame.
opening-image.craft: If your film is about a question, put the question in the title card. The audience will read every scene as evidence.
opening-image.craftTanglish: Unga padam oru kelviya patthinadhaa irundhaa, andha kelviya thodakkathuleye vachudunga. Ovvoru katchiyaiyum audience aadhaaramaa vaasippaanga.

theme-stated.inFilm: Stated by the folktale itself, before a live-action character speaks - every question has more than one defensible answer. The film does not put the theme in a mentor's mouth; it puts it in the structure.
theme-stated.inFilmTanglish: Nadodi kadhaiye theme-a solludhu - oru nadigar pesuradhukku munnaadiye. Ovvoru kelvikkum niyaayamaana oru badhilukku mela irukkum. Theme-a oru mentor vaayila padam vaikkala; amaippuleye vachudhu.
theme-stated.craft: A frame story can state your theme with no cost to the plot. It is the cheapest thematic statement available and almost nobody uses it.
theme-stated.craftTanglish: Oru frame kadhai, plot-ukku onnume selavaagaama unga theme-a sollidum. Kedaikkura mikka milivaana theme statement idhu thaan - kittathatta yaarume idha use panradhillai.

set-up.inFilm: The squad's moral untroubledness is the set-up. An encounter is performed and then tidied, and nobody in the room treats it as a problem. Establishing the wrong as normal is what gives the rest of the film something to disturb.
set-up.inFilmTanglish: Andha squad-oda arasiyal-thanmai kavalaiyinmai thaan set-up. Oru encounter nadakkudhu, appuram adha suththam pannuraanga; andha arailaye yaarum adha pirachanaiyaa paakkala. Thappa saadhaaranamaa nirupikkuradhu thaan, meedhi padathukku kalaikka edhaiyo kudukkudhu.
set-up.craft: Establish the wrong thing as routine, not as sin. A film cannot disturb a moral position the audience was never allowed to hold.
set-up.craftTanglish: Thappa paavamaa illa, vazhakkamaa nirupikkunga. Audience-a oru nilaipaattula nikka vidaama, andha nilaipaatta padathaala kalaikka mudiyaadhu.

catalyst.inFilm: The antagonist walks in and surrenders voluntarily. It is the best kind of catalyst - one the hero cannot refuse, cannot control, and did not cause.
catalyst.inFilmTanglish: Edhiri thaanaa ulle vandhu sarandaraan. Idhu thaan romba nalla vagai thoonduko - hero adha maruka mudiyaadhu, kattupaduththa mudiyaadhu, adhukku avan kaaranamum illa.
